text:
Elaine: heads-up — p99 latency jumped on a subset of us-west-g-1 hosts, ~220ms -> 1.2s starting ~16:30 UTC. I can see heavy KV cache churn and a lot of kernel swap churn in the logs. incbot alerted a few minutes ago.

incbot: INCIDENT detected: latency-surge on pool us-west-g-1 (p95 > 800ms). Runbook: /runbooks/kernel-thrash. Triage channel: #eng-runtime.

Rajesh: repro logs look like repeated kernel unload/load cycles every ~8-12s, plus frequent KV eviction bursts. Flamegraph shows time spent in kernel selection + context copy. snippet:
```
flamegraph: kernel_select 45%
             kvcache_evict 18%
             batch_pack 12%
```

Marta: throughput also dropped ~40% on the same pool. My hypothesis: batching heuristic oscillation — queue depth dips -> batches flush small -> kernel swap because of weird sequence length distribution. Looks like pipeline herding where many small requests from one tenant cause the scheduler to change kernels.

Ken: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) throttle noisy tenant T-443, 2) pin kernel mapping for affected pool to avoid swap churn, 3) disable prefetch heuristic on kvcache as a short-term. Commands: `redwoodctl tenants throttle set T-443 --rate=50rps` and `redwoodctl pools set kernel_policy=static --pool=us-west-g-1`.

Elaine: applying tenant throttle now (T-443 -> 50rps). Also toggling kvcache prefetch off: `redwoodctl config set kvcache.prefetch false --env=prod` — doing this on 3 hosts first.

Rajesh: attaching a tiny pprof summary I pulled off the hottest host:
```
# pprof top 5
12.8%  kernel_select
9.5%   memcpy_kv
7.3%   batch_dispatch
5.9%   quantize_path
3.4%   syscall_wait
```
Not huge CPU spike, but allocation churn + locks in kernel_select look suspicious.

Marta: routing plan: move heavy sessions to fallback_pool-usw-b for 20 minutes and enable canary static kernels on us-west-g-1. `routerctl route add --from=pool:us-west-g-1 --to=pool:fallback-usw-b --match=tenant:T-443 --weight=1`

Ken: after throttle + kvcache toggle, observed metrics: p50 ~180ms, p95 ~330ms, p99 still ~1.05s (some tails). I'll push static kernel pin for the pool: `redwoodctl pools kernel-pin enable --pool=us-west-g-1 --policy=pin-v1`

Elaine: toggled kernel-pin -> on for pool_usw_g_1. Also lowering max_batch_wait from 12ms -> 5ms for that pool to reduce batch size oscillation. `redwoodctl pools set batch.max_wait_ms=5 --pool=us-west-g-1`

sre-bot: paging oncall -> SRE-rotor@, escalation level: high. Add postmortem if incident persists beyond 1h.

Marta: follow-up experiment: we'll run two controlled changes: a) reduce max_batch_tokens 1024->512, b) raise batching jitter window to 8ms to avoid synchronized flushes. Will run on canary hosts (2 nodes) and report within 10m.

Rajesh: saving profiling artifacts to /var/tmp/prof-1975032468.tar.gz and uploading to the incident bucket (s3://redwood-incidents/1975032468/prof.tar.gz).

Ken: quick note — I've seen kernel selection regressions after last quantization patch; if static pin fixes this, we should consider reverting that kernel-chooser tweak or gating it behind a feature flag for now.

Elaine: monitoring window 30m from now. So far throttle + static pin + kvcache toggle improved p95/p50, p99 tail reduced by ~15%. If we see reoccurrence we'll escalate to a full postmortem. Thanks all — please add any logs/pprof links here. :thumbsup:
